explanation: Request is physically valid and required no correction. Eta photoproduction threshold is W_min = M_p + M_eta ≈ 0.938 + 0.548 = 1.486 GeV; the requested W range (1.55–1.75 GeV) lies comfortably above threshold. The EtaMAID-2023 hadronic model table used by this eta-channel build (mpintp.inc: NVAR1=101 covering Q2=0–5 GeV^2 in 0.05 GeV^2 steps; NVAR2=92 covering W=1.4856–6 GeV, with 10 MeV steps in 1.5–2.0 GeV) fully covers the requested W in [1.55,1.75] GeV and Q2 in [0.5,1.5] GeV^2 ranges, so no extrapolation outside the tabulated grid occurs. At the standard CLAS12 beam momentum (6.535 GeV) used in the eta-channel template, Q2 up to 1.5 GeV^2 at these W values requires only modest electron scattering angles (~12-13 degrees), well within the physically accessible range for this beam energy — Q2 is not artificially capped. cos(theta*)=0 and phi*=90 deg are both interior points of their physical domains ([-1,1] and [0,360] deg respectively). A 3x3 grid over (W,Q2) means the full factorial of 3 W values times 3 Q2 values = 9 kinematic points, each evaluated at the fixed cos(theta*)=0, phi*=90 deg; N=9 is within the 10-point-per-file Fortran reader limit, so a single-chunk input file suffices (no need for the multi-chunk/rcgrid_inputgen.py workflow). Used model=3 (maid2000/EtaMAID2023 slot), ivec=1 (recoil proton, correct for ep->e'p eta), lepton=1 (electron), rc_mode=0 (full O(alpha) radiative correction), and vcut=0.166 GeV^2 (the standard CLAS12 eta-analysis inelasticity cut), matching the documented eta-channel defaults in eta/input.dat and eta/examples/README.md. The trailing '0error...' sentinel line required by the legacy NAG-derived Fortran parser is included.
